source_text.body:
Teach topics by drawing on a shared canvas board
An agent connected over MCP draws, explains and sets exercises on a canvas so the user can learn physics, biology and geometry step by step.
·
Nov 9, 2026
Done with
GP
ChatGPT
What they did
The author built a free, open source macOS app with a canvas board. Any AI agent subscription connects to it over MCP. The agent sees the board, draws with sandboxed JavaScript and simulated ink, places three.js views, HTML and SVG, and receives updates on what the user changes. It is instructed to explain step by step and not give away answers to exercises. The author uses a drawing tablet and voice.
How it went
The author reports hours-long sessions learning physics, biology and geometry, starting from a broad question and going deeper. No measured results are given; Opus 5.5 on medium/high is called the best explainer so far.
Worth knowing
Hosted Gemini voice gives about 55 minutes per user per day and may run out of credits; otherwise install the local voice model from Settings.
Try it yourself
with
ChatGPT
Copy prompt
Teach me [topic, e.g. how levers work in physics] step by step at a [beginner/intermediate] level. Use the connected canvas to draw a diagram for each idea, explain it in a few sentences, then give me one short exercise to try before moving on. Stop after [number] steps with a short recap and a final quiz of three questions.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50425503
